new_scholarship.description: DAAD study scholarship for graduates in the arts to continue their education in Germany with a postgraduate or complementary course in Fine Art, Design, Visual Communication and Film. Funding covers a Master's/postgraduate degree course or a one-year complementary course without degree at a state or state-recognised German university. The scholarship pays a monthly stipend of EUR 992 plus a travel allowance, a one-off study allowance and insurance payments; it does not pay tuition fees. Selection is made by a DAAD specialist committee of professors from German art, design and film schools on the basis of the written application and the artistic portfolio.
new_scholarship.duration: 10 to 24 months for a Master's/postgraduate degree course; one academic year (usually 12 months) for complementary studies without degree

new_scholarship.description: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for students from abroad who want to study as undergraduate students at Japanese national universities, selected through the recommendation of a Japanese embassy or consulate general. Applicants first pass a First Screening (documents, written academic examinations and interview) at the diplomatic mission in their country, are recommended to MEXT, and then pass MEXT's Second Screening. The scholarship pays a monthly allowance of JPY 117,000, waives entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees, and provides an economy-class airline ticket to Japan and, on return, back to the grantee's home country. new_scholarship.description: Young Leaders Program (YLP) Students is the seventh type of the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship. new_scholarship.description: Kyushu University's own support programme for privately financed international students who come to Kyushu University on exchange, special auditing, special research or double degree status and who cannot afford to study in Japan solely at their own expense. It pays a monthly stipend of JPY 80,000, and the total of all scholarships held by the grantee may not exceed that amount. Applicants apply through their prospective host department at Kyushu University, not directly to the university centre. There are two recruitment periods per fiscal year: Period I around February for students who will study from April to September, and Period II around May for students who will study from October to March. The period of stay must be 3 months, 5 months (one semester) or 11 months (two semesters).

alerts.message: Kyushu University states that if you hold other scholarships, this award and your other funding combined will not exceed JPY 80,000 per month. Do not plan on receiving more than that in total.
You must return to your home university to obtain a degree or graduate. Students who complete a regular course of study at Kyushu University are not eligible for this scholarship.
The period of stay must be 3 months, 5 months (one semester) or 11 months (two semesters). Other durations are not funded.
As of 2026-10-04 both 2026 periods have passed. Period I, around February 2027, is for grantees starting between April and September 2027.
Kyushu University publishes two versions of this scholarship's amounts and duration. Confirm the applicable figures with your host department before applying.

submission_workflow: Choose the Kyushu University department you want to study in and confirm it will accept you as a special auditing, special research or double degree student
Contact that department's exchange programme officer or student affairs office to confirm the application method
Ask about the recruitment period that matches your intended start date
Prepare your transcript, grade evaluation coefficient, financial evidence and status documentation
Submit the application through the host department during Period I (around February) or Period II (around May)
Await the department's selection and the university's decision
Complete your studies at Kyushu University within 3, 5 or 11 months and return home to finish your degree
